n: A new figure enters: Kish, a respected and wealthy man from the small tribe of Benjamin. His family line is given to show he was a man of standing.

f.g: a man of wealth and influence

n: His son Saul is impressive to look at — handsome and a head taller than everyone else. He looks exactly like the kind of king the people wanted.

f.g: handsome, fine-looking

f.w: higher than any of the people

n: The story begins with something ordinary: Kish's donkeys wander off, and he sends Saul with a servant to find them. God often works through everyday events.

f.g: donkeys, valuable animals for work and travel

n: Saul and the servant search a wide area through several regions without finding the donkeys.

f.g: the hill country of Ephraim, north of Benjamin

n: Reaching the region of Zuph (Samuel's home area), Saul suggests going home before his father starts worrying more about them than the donkeys.

f.g: worry about us

n: The servant suggests visiting a respected man of God in the nearby town, whose words always come true. Perhaps he can tell them where to go. Interestingly, the servant knows of Samuel, but Saul does not.

f.w: all that he saith cometh surely to pass

n: Saul worries that they have no gift to bring, since their food is gone. It was customary to bring a present when visiting a prophet.
The servant has a quarter shekel of silver, a small gift he offers to give the man of God.

f.w: the fourth part of a shekel
f.g: A small weight of silver, perhaps around a tenth of an ounce.

n: A note for later readers: in earlier times a prophet was called a “seer,” one who sees. Latter-day Saints value this title, as the Lord designated Joseph Smith a seer.

f.g: One who sees spiritually; Hebrew ro'eh.

n: Saul agrees, and they head into the town where the man of God is.
On the way up the hill they meet young women going out to draw water and ask if the seer is there.

f.g: Wells and springs were usually outside the town, and drawing water was often women's work.

n: The young women tell them he has just arrived because there is a community sacrifice that day at the high place.

f.g: A hilltop worship site. Before the temple was built, these were sometimes used to worship the Lord; later they became associated with idolatry.

n: If they hurry, they will catch him before he goes up to bless the sacrifice; the meal cannot start until he blesses it.

f.g: Like a blessing on a meal, offered by the prophet before the feast.
invited

n: They enter the town just as Samuel is coming out toward them on his way to the high place. The timing is not accidental.

f.g: came out toward them, met them

n: The narrator reveals that the Lord had told Samuel about this meeting the day before.

f.g: revealed to him privately

n: God told Samuel to anoint a Benjaminite as leader to deliver Israel from the Philistines, because He had heard His people's cry. God grants the people's request, yet still cares for them.

f.g: Hebrew nagid — leader, ruler appointed by God; not yet the word “king.”

f.w: their cry is come unto me

n: When Saul appears, the Lord confirms to Samuel: this is the man who will rule God's people.

f.g: Literally “restrain” or “govern.”

n: Not recognizing Samuel, Saul asks him where the seer lives.
Samuel identifies himself and invites Saul to eat with him. He promises to tell Saul everything on his heart — hinting he knows more than Saul has said.
Samuel reassures Saul that the donkeys have been found, then hints at a far bigger matter: all Israel's hopes are focused on Saul and his family.

f.g: what Israel longs for — a king

n: Saul responds humbly: he is from Benjamin, the smallest tribe, and his family is the least. His humility at this point is genuine and appealing.
Samuel seats Saul and his servant at the head of about thirty guests in the dining hall — a place of honor for a stranger.

f.g: a hall or dining room

n: Samuel tells the cook to bring the special portion he had reserved ahead of time.
The cook serves Saul the choice leg or thigh, which Samuel had saved for him. Being served the honored portion signals Saul's coming role.

f.g: Probably the thigh or leg, a portion of honor.

n: After the feast, Samuel talks privately with Saul on the flat rooftop, a common place to rest and talk in the evening.

f.g: talked, conversed
Houses had flat roofs used as living space.

n: At dawn Samuel calls Saul from the rooftop to send him on his way, and they walk out together.

f.g: daybreak, dawn

n: At the edge of town Samuel sends the servant ahead so he can give Saul a private message from God.
